claims.text: A stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure mediates the combination of low density, mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance in lightweight high-entropy alloys.
Stable, coherent nanoscale precipitates enhance mechanical strength.
Stable, coherent nanoscale precipitates enhance corrosion resistance.
Stable, coherent nanoscale precipitates enhance high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The precipitate structure minimizes increases in alloy density.
Controlled additions of Ti, Al, or Cr can modify the microstructure and properties of a lightweight high-entropy alloy.
High-temperature annealing or aging can stabilize the nanoscale precipitate structure.
The relevant structural mediator includes coherent nanoscale precipitates and grain-boundary precipitates.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates strengthen the alloy by obstructing dislocation motion.
The precipitate structure reduces grain-boundary energy.
Reducing grain-boundary energy contributes to improved corrosion and oxidation resistance.
The precipitate structure inhibits corrosion reactions.
The precipitate structure inhibits high-temperature oxidation reactions.
An alloy containing the stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure will have greater mechanical strength than a baseline alloy lacking that structure.
An alloy containing the stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure will have greater corrosion resistance than the baseline alloy.
An alloy containing the stable, coherent nanoscale precipitate structure will have greater high-temperature oxidation resistance than the baseline alloy.
The precipitate-containing alloy will maintain low density relative to the baseline alloy.
Coarse or incoherent precipitates can degrade the targeted properties and terminate the hypothesized benefit.
The exact composition and processing conditions needed to form the proposed stable, coherent nanoscale precipitates are unknown.
Failure to improve strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance, or a significant density increase, would falsify the hypothesis.
